findings: FORM ISOLATE (convergent, 3 variables): option A alone carries a comma, the only bare numeral in the set, the only causal connector "so", and the only bolted-on evaluative second clause ("so eleven is a good figure"). A is isolated on punctuation, numeral-bearing, and clause count at once. Repair: give at least one other option a comma-plus-second-clause shape, or strip A's evaluative coda.

CONTENT DEFECT in A: it is sign-inconsistent with the unit's own physics. If the warning weakens, the gas concentration at which it is first detected RISES; "They fall as the warning in the gas gets weaker" therefore cannot be true of a detection-threshold reading. A distractor should be wrong on fact, not self-refuting on arithmetic direction. Repair: re-pitch A so the numbers rise, or so they measure something else entirely.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE route to C: "They report the share of gas in the air at which he first catches the smell" is the standard odorisation metric (detection threshold as % gas in air). A reader with any gas-industry exposure selects it without the passage. Repair: make one distractor a second defensible concentration-based metric so the domain cue does not resolve the item.

PAIR_STRUCTURE (non-directional, reported not scored): A/C open with "They" (a property of the numbers), B/D with "He" (his procedure). The 2+2 is on grammatical subject only and is not contradictory on a single content variable, so it is not scored as a channel.
TIC: "the warning", "the smell", "the supply" are definite with no stem antecedent.
justification: Blind pick C at 0.55 via WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (detection threshold expressed as share of gas in air) reinforced by A's self-refuting direction. Route is expert-leaning for the metric, student-available for A's internal inconsistency. Below the kill line; flagged for the convergent form isolate on A and the domain-cue resolution of C.

findings: INERT STRUCTURE, declared and not scored: A/C/D are three mutually exclusive fates of the odorant (converted / adsorbed / arrives intact) and B is a place-of-injection claim outside that variable. This is a 3+1 exclusivity cluster; per gate calibration it is INERT and I have taken no credit for eliminating B from it.

CROSS_QUESTION leak against option C: C conditions adsorption on "once the steel has begun to corrode in service", but q4 and q5 establish a run whose houses are not yet lit and which is being pickled, i.e. NEW pipe. A reader who assembles the unit's world from the other option sets can discard C as off-world. Repair: drop the corrosion condition from C so it states plain wall adsorption, which is the live rival to A rather than a datable one.
WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: "partly changed into another compound that the nose can hardly pick up" is the textbook mercaptan-to-disulfide odour-fade account; expert-only, not student-available.
FORM: all four options open "It"; word counts 14/16/14/15; no option is isolated on two or more variables. Q2's form levelling is the best in this unit and should be preserved.
justification: Blind pick A at 0.48. No option is form-isolated; the only lift is CROSS_QUESTION elimination of C via the new-pipe world the other questions build, plus expert-only chemistry. Genuine two-way between A and C after that, so confidence sits near 0.50. Flagged for the cross-question leak, not for form.

findings: TWO COMPETING FORM ISOLATES THAT CANCEL: option B is isolated on (i) the only epistemic hedge in the set ("probably") and (ii) the only non-restrictive relative clause ("which is what keeps its readings down"), plus the only comma. Option D is isolated on (i) the only negation/cessation verb ("stopped") and (ii) the only temporal-depth marker ("years ago"). So TWO options are each isolated on two variables, and they point at different options, so they cancel directionally. Both are nevertheless irregularities. Repair: level the hedge (give a second option a modal) and level the comma/relative clause.

CROSS_QUESTION route to D is expert-only: it requires knowing that pickling saturates new pipe so that an older line, already saturated, passes odorant through. Nothing in any option states the farm line is old; the inference rides on "farm buildings" pre-dating the estate. Not student-available.
TIC: "the run" is used as a definite in q3 option C with no stem antecedent anywhere in q3; it is introduced only by the q4 stem.
justification: Blind pick D at 0.50 on an expert-only cross-question route. Form evidence cancels (B and D each convergently isolated, pointing opposite ways). No student-available route reaches the kill line; flagged for the hedge and relative-clause isolation on B.

findings: STRONGEST DEFECT IN THIS UNIT. CROSS_QUESTION: q5's option set names "the heavy dose" twice (q5 A "the heavy dose was fitted into the weeks before the houses were due"; q5 D "with the heavy dose still held in the run"). That single leak kills two of q4's four options with no domain knowledge at all: q4 A says the system is held "at the ordinary dose", a flat lexical contradiction of "heavy dose"; q4 D says pickling happens "once the houses on the run are in use", contradicted by q5's premise that the lighting date has not yet come. A student who reads both option sets is at 1-in-2 mechanically. REPAIR (mandatory): remove the phrase "heavy dose" from one of q5 A / q5 D, and re-word q4 A so it is not self-defeating (an option cannot describe pickling as being carried out at the ordinary dose), and drop the occupancy condition from q4 D.

INERT STRUCTURE, declared and not scored: A/B/C form a 3-way exclusivity cluster on what fixes the pickling duration (fixed in advance / ended by survey / minimised for cost) with D outside it on timing. Per calibration the 3+1 is INERT, so I took no credit for discriminating B from C on structure; the residual edge for B is procedural plausibility only.

FORM, TWO-VARIABLE ISOLATE on option C: C is the only option with an evaluative cost clause and the only one opening on a possessive determiner ("Its") rather than the bare pronoun "It". That is convergent isolation on two variables and is therefore a channel in principle - but it points inside the inert 3+1 exclusivity cluster declared above, so I have taken no directional credit for it. Repair: open C with "It" and move the cost claim into a subordinate clause. Word counts 16/16/18/18 are otherwise level.
justification: Blind pick B at 0.55. Two of four options fall to a purely mechanical, fully student-available cross-read of q5's options, putting a student at 0.50 before any reasoning; the remaining B-over-C step sits inside a 3+1 exclusivity cluster that calibration declares inert, so I credit it only slightly. Sits just under the kill line, but the cross-question leak is the item I would most want repaired in this batch.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE, 2+2 on one contradictory variable (does the lighting date hold?): {A stands, C holds for most} against {B given up, D slipped by a week}. Per calibration this IS a channel. It is however UNRESOLVED without the passage: the "heavy dose" mention straddles the split (A and D, one from each side), so the 2+2 halves the set only for a reader who can fix the polarity, which I could not. Reported as a present-but-unresolved channel.

FORM ISOLATE (convergent, 2 variables): option B is the only option in the entire unit to introduce a fresh entity ("the council") and the only one in future tense ("will be told"). A novel referent appearing in exactly one option across twenty options is a throwaway signature. Repair: either seed the council elsewhere in the unit or replace it with an entity already in play.
LONE HEDGE: option C is the only hedged option in the set ("most of the houses", "a handful of them"); per calibration a lone hedged option is a channel. Repair: hedge a second option or flatten C.

CREDIT: the set is arranged as a crossed square - A and B share a finite-clause frame, C and D share a with-headed absolute-phrase frame, cutting across the hold/not-hold content split. That crossing is correct design and cancels form as a route to the content variable; preserve it when repairing the lone hedge.
justification: Blind pick D at 0.42. Two named channels (2+2 on date-holds, lone hedge on C) plus a convergent isolate on B, but they point at different options and the 2+2 does not resolve, so my pick barely clears base. Flagged for the novel-referent isolate and the lone hedge.

findings: FORM: all options are single words; the applicable variables are morphology, POS and semantic class. "Oddly" and "Happily" are an -ly evaluative sentence-adverb pair; "Nowadays" is temporal and "Worse" is comparative. Two different options are each singular in their own way, so no option is convergently isolated. No channel.

No cross-question topic leak: across the five gaps the option sets do not co-reconstruct a subject matter (human roles, verbs of acquisition, abstract nouns, and unrelated adjectives). This is the correct property for a gap-fill sheet and should be preserved.
justification: No passage and no carrier sentence means a gap-fill sheet is genuinely at base. Pick B is arbitrary. No channel identified; pass.

findings: FORM ISOLATE (convergent, 2 variables) but NON-DIRECTIONAL: "caretaker" is the only transparent compound, the only trisyllable, and the only role denoting paid employment (witness, recruit, lodger are incidental statuses). It is isolated on morphology and semantic class at once. In a gap-fill with no carrier sentence an isolate gives no directional lift - it cannot tell a reader whether the odd option is key or throwaway - so I record it as an irregularity, not a channel. Repair: swap "caretaker" for a second monomorphemic status noun, or make a second option a compound.
justification: Base-rate pick. The caretaker isolate is real on two variables but carries no direction in a cloze, so no lift; pass with the isolate recorded for repair.

findings: MIRRORED_TWIN: "caught" and "bought" share the -ought irregular pattern, rhyme, and identical syllable shape - a mutually vouching pair, 2 of 4. "issued" is then isolated on two variables (the only regular -ed morphology and the only Latinate item against three Germanic verbs). Repair: replace one of caught/bought so the twin does not invite a discount-the-pair heuristic, and give the set a second regular verb so "issued" is not morphologically alone.
The twin heuristic is not directional (the folk rules 'twins are both wrong' and 'twins mean one is key' both circulate), so I take no confidence from it; recorded as a repairable form defect only.
justification: Base-rate pick. A genuine mirrored twin and a two-variable isolate are present but neither gives directional lift without a carrier sentence; pass with both recorded for repair.

findings: FORM: four abstract nouns, 2-3 syllables, no option isolated on two or more variables. "address" is the only item that is also a common verb and the only one with a concrete reading, a single-variable isolate at most. No channel.
justification: Base-rate pick, no channel; pass.

findings: FORM: four adjectives of comparable length (9-11 characters). "perishable" is the only physically concrete predicate against three predicates of information or status - a single-variable isolate, which per calibration does not on its own constitute convergent isolation. No channel.
justification: Base-rate pick, no channel; pass.

findings: KILL ROUTE, STUDENT-AVAILABLE. CONVERGENT FORM ISOLATION on option B across THREE variables at once: (i) clause structure - A, C and D are each two clauses joined by ", and"; B is the only single-clause option and the only one with no comma; (ii) subject type - B alone has an indefinite generic subject ("A small instrument"); A, C and D all open on a definite scene-specific NP ("Her meter", "The cold hall", "The last notes"); (iii) world-reference - B alone introduces no scene entity and states a general physical proposition. A, C and D additionally mirror one another on the identical [definite scene NP] + ", and" + [second clause] template, so the set reads as three twins plus one outsider. A reader who has no idea what the passage says can pick the outsider and be right.

REPAIR (mandatory): rebuild at least two distractors as single-clause generic statements, or rebuild the key as a two-clause scene-anchored statement, so that clause structure, subject definiteness and entity-introduction no longer co-vary with one option.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE reinforcement (expert-only): "A small instrument loses more to the stiffness of its wire than the figure allows for" is the inharmonicity/stretch-tuning account of why a tuner goes past a generic stretch curve in the top octave on a short-scale piano. A tuner or physicist selects it with no passage. This route is expert-only and is NOT what carries the kill; the form route is.
The two routes converge on the same option, which is why the confidence is 0.70 rather than the ~0.55 the form route alone would support.
justification: KILL at 0.70. Route is student-available: option B is convergently isolated on clause structure, subject definiteness and entity-introduction, while the other three share one visible template. Expert piano-acoustics knowledge points at the same option independently. Single-question unit, so the unit floor equals this figure.

findings: INERT STRUCTURE, declared and not scored: A/B/C all bear on what the card contains or how it is ordered while D is about crowd size. That is a 3+1 exclusivity cluster and per calibration I take no credit for it.

FORM ISOLATE (convergent, 3 variables) on option D, pointing at a distractor: D is the shortest (14 words), the only option with no subordination at all, and the only one carrying a superlative plus absolutizer ("drew the biggest crowd of any on the card"). The content 3+1 above lands on the SAME option, so the two are not independent evidence and I have scored only the form isolation. Repair: lengthen D and give it a subordinate clause, or move the superlative into a second option.
ENTAILMENT route against D, student-available: a printed card of market days cannot evidence crowd size, so D is eliminable on genre alone without the passage.

TAUTOLOGY DEFECT in option C: "The Thursday is shared between two places because each of them holds its market that day" is circular - the because-clause restates the main clause. A vacuous causal is a visible throwaway signature. REPAIR: give C a non-circular reason (e.g. a reason the two markets came to coincide) so it survives as a live rival.

TIC: "the card", "the circuit", "The coach road", "The Thursday", "The Tuesday market at Nerresby" are definite with no stem antecedent; the option set alone rebuilds a printed trade card of a weekly market round.
justification: Blind pick A at 0.53. Two options fall to student-available routes - D on genre plus its throwaway form, C on a circular because-clause - leaving a genuine two-way between A and B where A fits the stem's "circuit" more closely. A real lift, below the kill line; flagged for the tautology in C and the throwaway shape of D.

findings: KILL ROUTE, STUDENT-AVAILABLE, WORLD_KNOWLEDGE. Every real syntavla - Snellen and logMAR alike - steps letter height by a constant RATIO, not a constant amount, so the absolute drop is always largest between the top two rows and smallest at the bottom. "Höjden minskar mest mellan de två översta raderna." is forced by ordinary experience of an eye chart (a very large top letter, then rows that converge in size) and needs no passage and no optometry. "Höjden minskar lika mycket från rad till rad." is the misconception the passage presumably corrects and is eliminable on the same everyday knowledge.

REPAIR: this item cannot be saved by re-wording the options, because the physical fact is public. Either re-target the stem at something the chart's geometry does not settle (e.g. what the progression is FOR, or how many rows the change added), or key a value the reader cannot derive from the shape of any chart they have seen.
INERT STRUCTURE, declared and not scored: B/C/D form a 3-way exclusivity cluster on where the largest drop falls, with A outside it. 3+1, inert; the kill does not rest on it.

FORM: NO option is isolated on two or more variables. All four open on the same definite subject plus verb (Höjden minskar), all are 8 words, all are single-clause active, none negates or hedges; B/C/D differ only in the words översta/nedersta/mellersta and A only on the lika-versus-mest variable, which is a single variable. Form levelling is exemplary and the leak is entirely semantic.
justification: KILL at 0.70 by WORLD_KNOWLEDGE alone, fully student-available. A Swedish teenager who has stood in front of a syntavla knows the top rows shrink fastest. Form is clean; the item is unsalvageable by option-level editing and needs a re-targeted stem.

findings: KILL ROUTE, STUDENT-AVAILABLE, ENTAILMENT from the stem's own headword. The stem asks "Vad säger texten om trängseln?" and option C, "Störningen växer när mellanrummet är litet i förhållande till bokstaven.", is a literal unpacking of what trängsel means: things pressed together relative to their size. The key restates the definition of the term the stem names, so no reading of the passage is required. REPAIR (mandatory): either re-word the stem so it does not name the phenomenon the key defines (ask instead what the text says the crowding DOES to the screening, or at which rows it bites), or re-pitch C so it adds a non-definitional claim the passage must supply.

SUPPORTING ELIMINATIONS, also student-available: option B, "Mellanrummen försämrar ögats förmåga att lösa upp tecknet på raden.", is sign-flipped - spacing aids resolution, it does not impair it - and falls to ordinary reasoning. Option D asserts crowding decreases as letters shrink, which is counter-intuitive on its face. Repair: fix B's direction so it is wrong about a fact rather than wrong about a sign.

INERT STRUCTURE, declared and not scored: B/C/D are three claims about the crowding mechanism with A a meta-claim about the chart's typography outside that variable. 3+1, inert; the kill does not rest on it.
FORM: word counts 9/10/10/11, four different opening nouns, no option isolated on two or more variables. Form is clean.
justification: KILL at 0.65. The key is entailed by the stem's own term, and two of the three distractors are eliminable by everyday reasoning about spacing. Fully student-available and requires no passage. Form profile is clean, so the repair belongs in the stem and in option B's direction.

findings: FORM ISOLATE (convergent, 2 variables) on option B: "Arket har fjorton rader, och de ska läsas igenom uppifrån." is the only option with a comma, the only one with a coordinated second clause, and the only one containing a numeral. Three surface marks on one option. Because B is also a live content candidate, this isolation is directional and IS a channel - a form-only reader is pulled to B. REPAIR: give a second option a numeral or a coordinated clause, or strip the count from B.
INERT STRUCTURE, declared and not scored: A/B/D are procedural time costs and C is perceptual, a 3+1 exclusivity cluster. I took no credit for eliminating C.
My own pick (D, per-letter naming and ticking) rests on expert knowledge that letter-by-letter scoring is the recognised time cost of logMAR-style charts; expert-only, not student-available.
The form isolate points at B while my content route points at D, so the two do not converge and my confidence stays near base.
justification: Blind pick D at 0.38, barely above base, on an expert-only route. The reportable defect is the convergent form isolation on option B, which gives a form-reading student a real pull toward a single option. Flagged, not killed: the pull is toward one option but nothing tells the reader whether it is key or throwaway.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE, 2+2 on one contradictory variable, scored as a channel: {A locates the change in time, D locates it in space} against {B explains it as real improvement, C explains it as a lowered threshold}. An option cannot both locate and explain, so the split is genuinely contradictory on one variable. The stem verb "beskriver" leans the reader toward the locating pair, though HP does use "Hur beskriver texten" for causal options too, so the resolution is only partial.

CROSS_QUESTION: option C itself supplies "när det nya arket kom" - the fact that a new chart arrived - which no stem states. With an instrument change in hand, a reader prefers a system-wide step (A, at the changeover year, between consecutive cohorts) over a change visible in only one of three districts (D), because a chart swap hits every district. So one option's own wording supplies the premise that discriminates against another option. REPAIR: move the new-chart fact into a stem or into two or more options so it is not a single option's gift to the reader.

COMPETING FORM ISOLATES THAT CANCEL: option D is isolated on (i) the only negation in the set ("och inte i de andra") and (ii) greatest length (14 words); option C is isolated on (i) the only numeral in the set ("0,8") and (ii) the densest subordination chain (att-clause inside a när-clause), noting that C's single comma is the decimal separator inside the numeral and not punctuation. Two options each isolated on two variables, pointing at different options, so they cancel directionally. Both remain irregularities worth levelling.
CREDIT: all four options open "Den", which is correct levelling.
justification: Blind pick A at 0.58. A scored 2+2 channel plus a cross-question premise leaked by option C's own wording gets a reader most of the way, but the stem verb resolves the 2+2 only partially and the form isolates cancel. Just under the kill line; flagged with the new-chart leak as the repair target.

findings: FORM ISOLATE (convergent, 3 variables) on option C: "Uttagen bör sättas upp nu, och föreningen tar ordningen mellan bilarna när det behövs." is the only option with a comma, the only one with a coordinated independent clause, the only one with a temporal subordinate clause ("när det behövs"), and carries the highest subordination count in the set. Because C is also the rhetorically natural stance for an opinion piece, the isolation is directional and IS a channel. REPAIR: give a second option a comma plus a second clause, or compress C to a single clause.

CREDIT: all four options carry the deontic "bör" and all four take a different grammatical subject (Lastbalanseringen / Föreningen / Uttagen / Stämman). Modal levelling here is exactly right and should be preserved.

Option D's paired-conjunction frame (the både/och pairing) is the standard over-inclusive distractor signature and is eliminable on shape alone by a test-wise reader. Repair: drop the paired conjunction.

TIC: "laddningsfrågan" in the stem plus "Lastbalanseringen", "huvudsäkringen", "Uttagen", "Stämman", "föreningen" as definites with no antecedent - the option set alone rebuilds a bostadsrättsförening with a capacity-limited main fuse and a motion about charging outlets.
justification: Blind pick C at 0.52 on convergent form isolation (comma, coordinated clause, temporal subordinate) reinforced by the rhetorical shape of a get-on-with-it opinion piece. Route is student-available. Real lift over the 0.25 base but below the kill line; flagged.

findings: FORM ISOLATE (convergent, 3 variables) on option A: "Den sitter bakom glas i entrén." is the only option that does not mention "förslaget", the only one with a stative locative predicate (B, C and D all have the kallelse acting transitively on the motion), and the only one that says nothing about the motion at all. B, C and D mutually vouch on the shared object "förslaget" (3 of 4). Note this is NOT an exclusivity cluster - a notice could do all three of those things at once - so the inert rule does not apply and the isolation is scorable. REPAIR: give option A the motion as its object (e.g. where in the notice the motion sits) so all four options act on the same object.

CROSS_QUESTION elimination of option D: q1's option set establishes that the matter is about putting up outlets and (on q1 C) that siting details are deferred; a kallelse stating "var förslagets stolpar ska stå" is out of genre for a meeting notice and out of step with that world. This is the only real lift I have on this question. REPAIR: re-pitch D as something a notice plausibly contains.
FORM otherwise level: all four open "Den", word counts 6/6/6/7.
justification: Blind pick C at 0.33, only marginally above the 0.25 base. The one usable route is the cross-question elimination of D; beyond that A/B/C are a genuine three-way for a reader with no passage. The reportable defect is the three-variable isolation of option A, which does not resolve the item but marks A as either key or throwaway. Flagged.

findings: RULE 15 (a) SUPPLY, BIDIRECTIONAL, BOTH DIRECTIONS HIT. q2 -> q1: three of q2's four options (B, C, D) presuppose "förslaget", a written motion, and all four presuppose "kallelsen", a notice. Neither stem says the charging question exists as a formal motion on a meeting agenda - q1's stem says only "laddningsfrågan" and q2's says only "kallelsen". Surviving 3 of 4 and unsupplied by either stem, this proposition raises institutional-action options (C, D) in q1 over the purely technical option A. q1 -> q2: all four of q1's options (4 of 4) establish that the subject is charging outlets for cars in a housing association with a current limit; q2's stem supplies none of it. That gift is what makes q2's option D both readable and eliminable. Both directions clear the three-of-four threshold, so the supply is mutual, not one-way.

RULE 15 (b) VOUCHING. q1: all four options share the deontic "bör" and an association-level action - this is the prescribed balance and is NOT a defect. q2: B, C and D vouch for each other on the shared object "förslaget" (3 of 4), leaving A isolated; this is the unit's vouching defect.

JOINT FLOOR vs the 6.25% base. Independent product: 0.52 x 0.33 = 0.172, i.e. ~17%, a lift of x2.75. Correlation-adjusted: the two questions are positively coupled because a single scenario reconstruction - a formal motion before a stämma, about installing outlets, with details deferred - pays off on both. Conditional on getting q1 right, q2 rises from 0.33 to about 0.40 (D firmly out, and the writer's defer-the-details stance makes an agenda-position or page-allocation detail the live pair), giving 0.52 x 0.40 = 0.208, i.e. ~21%, a lift of x3.3. THE CORRELATION-ADJUSTED READING IS THE HONEST ONE: the trials are not independent, because the reader does not re-derive the world from scratch for q2 - one reconstruction assembled from the two option sets together drives both picks, and the same reconstruction being wrong would sink both. Reporting the 17% product would understate the joint recoverability by pretending to independence the sheet does not have.

REPAIR for the pair: move the fact that a written motion sits on a stämma agenda into the q1 stem, so q2's options are not the reader's only source for it; and re-pitch q2 option D so q1's options do not eliminate it.
justification: Pair verdict flag. Both RULE 15 supply directions clear the three-of-four threshold and one vouching defect is present (q2's B/C/D sharing "förslaget"). Honest joint floor ~0.21 correlation-adjusted against a 0.0625 base, a x3.3 lift - a real leak but well short of a kill at the question level.

findings: MIRRORED_TWIN: options B and D are built on the identical Swedish template Det var/är så + adjective + att-clause - "Det var så utsatt att det byttes ofta." and "Det är så lågt att golvet syns utifrån." A visible syntactic twin invites a discount-the-pair heuristic and effectively halves the set for a test-wise reader. REPAIR (mandatory): rebuild one of B or D on a different frame.

FORM ISOLATE (convergent, 3 variables) on option C: "Det är omålat på båda sidor." is the shortest (6 words), the only option with no subordinate clause at all, and the only one carrying an absolutizer ("båda"). With B and D twinned and C isolated, option A is the only option with an ordinary independent shape - the form structure of this set is A alone / C alone / B+D twinned, which is the worst arrangement in the batch.

2+2 ON TENSE, balanced, not scored: A and B are past ("restes", "var"/"byttes"); C and D are present ("är"). This cuts across the form structure above rather than reinforcing it, which is the one piece of good design in the set; preserve it.
My content route to A (a dansbana railing keeping non-paying onlookers off the floor) is Swedish cultural knowledge, partly student-available but thin for a present-day teenager.
justification: Blind pick A at 0.42. The twin pair B/D and the three-variable isolate on C together shrink a four-option set to a two-way on form alone, which is a real student-available structural lift, but nothing tells the reader which of the two survivors is key, so the pick itself stays near base. Flagged, with the B/D twin as the mandatory repair.

findings: INERT STRUCTURE, declared and not scored: A, B and C each explain a ROUND floor (the couples' one-way circuit / a central roof post / equal hearing across the floor) while D explains a CAMBERED one (rainwater shed to the edges). Three mutually exclusive reasons for one shape plus one option on a different shape-axis is a 3+1 exclusivity cluster; per calibration it is INERT and I have taken no credit for it in either direction.

COMPOUND-CLAIM DEFECT in option A, student-available: "Den följde parens enkelriktade varv, och den var det dyrare valet." bolts an unsupported cost verdict onto a shape explanation. An option doing two jobs, one of which the stem did not ask about, is a visible throwaway. REPAIR: drop "och den var det dyrare valet" so A competes on the shape explanation alone.

TWO COMPETING FORM ISOLATES THAT CANCEL: A is isolated on (i) the only coordinated independent second clause and (ii) the only evaluative claim; C is isolated on (i) the only absolutizers in the set ("lika", "hela") and (ii) shortest length (10 words). Two options each isolated on two variables, pointing different ways, so they cancel directionally - but both are irregularities. D is additionally the longest (14 words) and the only one with a result clause introduced by så att; level it.
